task.title: Protocol-safe reset auto-pickup and agency levels
task.summary: Implement CodeWiki reset auto-pickup from source-backed protocol-safe kickoff messages and add configurable task/sprint/roadmap agency levels that govern continuation.

goal.outcome: CodeWiki reset auto-picks up through a protocol-safe source-backed kickoff when configured agency level allows continuation; agency level task/sprint/roadmap controls approval cadence while hard gates remain mandatory.
acceptance: Same-session CodeWiki compaction delivers a minimal resume-context kickoff with auto turn triggering when safe.
Fresh-session resume seeds the replacement session with the same source-backed kickoff while preserving manual /wiki-resume UX.
Reset defers or refuses auto-pickup when pending tool/message state or adapter capability cannot guarantee a valid next-turn boundary.
No reset path injects slash-command text through follow-up chat or calls continuation from an assistant-role leaf.
Regression tests reproduce invalid assistant-leaf risk and prove safe kickoff/fallback behavior.
Config schema/defaults expose agency level, approval cadence, context reset auto-pickup, budgets, and hard stop gates.
Agency planner interprets task, sprint, and roadmap levels as continuation boundaries, not permission to bypass validation/risk/publication/destructive gates.
Status/config surfaces show effective agency level and reset auto-pickup policy.
Roadmap-level agency remains budgeted and stops on semantic decisions, validation blocks, artifact conflicts, risk escalation, publication/destructive actions, or unsafe reset boundaries.
non_goals: Do not implement parallel subagent orchestration unless already supported by existing agency machinery.
Do not grant automatic publication or remote push permission.
Do not publish or push changes.

exit_criteria: Observed assistant-leaf continuation error is addressed by protocol-safe kickoff delivery.
Regression tests fail if reset auto-pickup uses nextTurn with triggerTurn.
Fresh implementation validation starts from source refs and content proof.
